t:
(a) In General.—Chapter 7 of title 10, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following new section:“§ 187. Strategic Materials Protection Board“(a) Establishment.—(1) The Secretary of Defense shall establish a Strategic Materials Protection Board.“(2) The Board shall be composed of representatives of the following:“(A) The Secretary of Defense, who shall be the chairman of the Board.“(B) The Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition, Technology, and Logistics.“(C) The Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence.“(D) The Secretary of the Army.“(E) The Secretary of the Navy.“(F) The Secretary of the Air Force.“(b) Duties.—In addition to other matters assigned to it by the Secretary of Defense, the Board shall—“(1) determine the need to provide a long term domestic supply of materials designated as critical to national security to ensure that national defense needs are met;“(2) analyze the risk associated with each material designated as critical to national security and the effect on national defense that the nonavailability of such material from a domestic source would have;“(3) recommend a strategy to the President to ensure the domestic availability of materials designated as critical to national security;“(4) recommend such other strategies to the President as the Board considers appropriate to strengthen the industrial base with respect to materials critical to national security; and“(5) publish not less frequently than once every two years in the Federal Register recommendations regarding materials critical to national security, including a list of specialty metals, if any, recommended for addition to, or removal from, the definition of ‘specialty metal’ for purposes of section 2533b of this title.“(c) Meetings.—The Board shall meet as determined necessary by the Secretary of Defense but not less frequently than once every two years to make recommendations regarding materials critical to national security as described in subsection (b)(5).“(d) Reports.—After each meeting of the Board, the Board shall prepare and submit to Congress a report containing the results of the meeting and such recommendations as the Board determines appropriate.”
. 
    (b) Clerical Amendment.—The table of sections at the beginning of such chapter is amended by adding at the end the following new item:


“187. 
Strategic Materials Protection Board.”.

 
    (c) First Meeting of Board.—The first meeting of the Strategic Materials Protection Board, established by section 187 of title 10, United States Code (as added by subsection (a)) shall be not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that a "Board" that publishes recommendations in the Federal Register and reports its results is a participatory body. But every member represents a Department of Defense official, so the Board sits entirely inside the federal government, and its recommendations go to the President and Congress, who are also inside it. Publishing recommendations in the Federal Register is one-way disclosure, not a comment period or rulemaking, and no outside party is consulted or given a right to object or sue.
fable.s: The Board shall be composed of representatives of the following:“(A) The Secretary of Defense, who shall be the chairman of the Board.“(B) The Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition, Technology, and Logistics.

qwen_block.w: The Strategic Materials Protection Board is composed entirely of high-ranking federal officials (Secretaries and Under Secretaries of Defense and the military branches). Since all members are inside the federal government, there is no participation by outside parties such as the public, states, or private entities. The board's duties involve internal analysis and reporting to the President and Congress, which are intra-governmental actions.

(B) The Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition, Technology, and Logistics. (C) The Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence. (D) The Secretary of the Army. (E) The Secretary of the Navy. opus.w: The Strategic Materials Protection Board is made up only of Defense Department officials, so its meetings and recommendations involve coordination within the federal government. Publishing recommendations in the Federal Register is a notice requirement, not a comment period, and the reports go to Congress, which is also inside the federal government. The words 'Board', 'meetings' and 'Federal Register' are tempting, but no state, expert, company or member of the public takes part in any federal decision.

opus.b:
**Tempting but wrong reading:** This section creates a "Board," requires it to hold "Meetings," and has it publish recommendations in the Federal Register. That sounds like an advisory body and a public process.

**Why it fails:** Every Board member is a federal official: the Secretary of Defense, two Under Secretaries of Defense, and the Secretaries of the Army, Navy and Air Force. The meetings are internal, not public hearings. Publishing in the Federal Register only announces the recommendations; it opens no comment period. The reports go to Congress, which is inside the federal government. No one outside the federal government takes part.

qwen_chat.w: The Strategic Materials Protection Board is composed entirely of federal officials (Secretaries and Under Secretaries of Defense and the military services). Because all members are inside the federal government, the board's activities constitute intra-governmental coordination rather than participation with outside parties. The reports generated are submitted to Congress, which is also part of the federal government, so no external consultation or public participation is required.

(B) The Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition, Technology, and Logistics. (C) The Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence. (D) The Secretary of the Army. (E) The Secretary of the Navy. (F) The Secretary of the Air Force.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: The section establishes a "Board" and requires it to make recommendations, which might suggest participation if the board included outside experts or stakeholders. However, looking closely at subsection (a)(2), the board is composed entirely of high-ranking federal officials (Secretary of Defense, Under Secretaries, Service Secretaries). Since all members are inside the federal government, this is intra-governmental coordination, not participation with outside parties. The reports are submitted to Congress, which is also inside the federal government. Therefore, no outside party is involved in the decision-making process described.
